name: Refactoring Guru
description: Illustrated catalog of design patterns, refactoring techniques, and code smells.
why: The fastest vocabulary for naming a structural problem before changing code.

name: Martin Fowler
description: Foundational writing on refactoring, architecture, domain modeling, and evolutionary design.
why: Primary source for concepts agents often cite incorrectly.

name: System Design Primer
description: Open-source guide to large-scale system design with diagrams and tradeoffs.
why: A broad, well-maintained reference for architecture conversations.

name: C4 Model
description: A hierarchical way to diagram software architecture: context, containers, components, code.
why: Gives agents and humans a shared diagram vocabulary that stays readable.

name: Architecture Decision Records
description: Lightweight templates and conventions for recording architectural decisions.
why: Keeps the reason behind a choice attached to the codebase.

name: Best Dead Code Detection Tools (2026)
description: Language-by-language comparison of dead-code tools: Knip, Vulture, deadcode, deptry, ts-prune, Go deadcode, PMD, PHPStan, cargo-machete, and repowise.
why: A current, method-backed map of which dead-code tool to use for each stack.

name: Knip
description: Finds unused files, exports, and dependencies in JavaScript and TypeScript projects, including monorepos.
why: The strongest open-source dead-code tool for JS/TS, with 200+ framework plugins and auto-fix.

name: Vulture
description: Python dead-code finder with confidence scores and whitelist support.
why: The standard Python starting point for unused code.

name: deadcode
description: Python dead-code detector with a `--fix` mode.
why: Useful when you want automated removal after reviewing a dry run.

name: deptry
description: Reports missing, unused, and misplaced Python dependencies.
why: Unused dependencies are dead code in the manifest; deptry covers them.

name: ts-prune
description: Prints unused exports from a TypeScript project.
why: Narrow but useful when you only need an export list.

name: dependency-cruiser
description: Validates and visualizes JavaScript/TypeScript dependency graphs and architectural rules.
why: Turns architecture boundaries into checks an agent can run.

name: madge
description: Generates dependency graphs and detects circular dependencies in JS/TS projects.
why: Fast way to expose cycles before a refactor.

name: jscpd
why: Finds duplicated logic that agents tend to create across files.

name: Semgrep
description: Pattern-based static analysis for security and code-quality rules across many languages.
why: Rules are readable and fast enough to run in an agent loop.

name: CodeQL
description: Semantic code analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.
why: Deep data-flow analysis for security issues in supported languages.

name: SonarQube
description: Continuous code-quality and security analysis with quality gates.
why: Useful when a team wants a shared gate rather than ad-hoc lint runs.

name: Andrej Karpathy Guidelines & Skills
description: Community-maintained coding guidelines inspired by Andrej Karpathy, covering surgical changes, explicit assumptions, and verifiable outcomes.
why: Essential behavioral guardrail for vibe coding agents to avoid unnecessary abstractions and surface hidden assumptions.

name: Docker build best practices
description: Docker documents multi-stage builds, base image choice, dependency management and Dockerfile instructions.
why: Evaluate the build stages, final image contents and base image before releasing a container.
